title: risk-management-service posture aggregation pipeline matches on both organizationId and projectId in every $match/$group stage
description: analytics.job.ts's calculatePostureForOrgProject(organizationId, projectId) explicitly converts both IDs to ObjectId and includes both in its $match stages (verified at lines ~145-158). This test verifies the end-to-end aggregation output for one {org, project} pair never includes counts contributed by a sibling project or another organization's risk records.
preconditions: Org A has Project X (5 risks) and Project Y (3 risks)
Org B has Project Z (10 risks)
steps: Trigger posture calculation for Org A / Project X
Inspect the resulting PostureSnapshot risk counts
expectedResult: Snapshot reflects exactly 5 risks (Project X's own count) — never 8 (X+Y combined) and never any contribution from Org B's Project Z.

title: Centralised /tasks aggregation applies organizationId across all 8 internal MongoDB sources plus the 3 microservice fan-out calls
description: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/tasks/tasks.service.js post-filters WorkflowEntry results by resolving org scope via the entity model (WorkflowEntry has no native organizationId field) and passes { userId, organizationId } as serviceParams to microservice fan-out calls (risk-management-service, vendor-service, trust-vault-service via internal-tasks.routes.ts). This verifies no source in the fan-out leaks another org's tasks into the aggregated response.
preconditions: Org A and Org B each have open tasks across at least 3 of the 9 entity types (e.g. AuditScopeItem, Finding, VendorAssessment, Risk)
steps: As an org A user, call GET /tasks
Enumerate every returned task's underlying organizationId (via its source module) for all 9 entity types
expectedResult: Every task in the response belongs to org A, across every one of the 8 internal sources and all 3 microservice fan-out results (risk-management-service, vendor-service, trust-vault-service). Any Promise.allSettled partial failure surfaces as an explicit `_partial` warning, not as silently-included cross-org data.

title: cap-evaluation.worker.js computes usage per organization without cross-org contribution when a $lookup or nested query is involved
description: cap-evaluation.worker.js consistently threads organizationId: org._id (or orgId) through its Project.findOne, User.find, and usage-count queries (verified at lines 66, 98, 121, 167). This test confirms the worker's computed usage figures for one org are unaffected by the total number of users/projects/vendors across all other tenants in the same run.
preconditions: Org B (much larger) has 200 users, 50 projects
Both orgs are evaluated in the same worker run
steps: Trigger the billing cap-evaluation worker for both orgs in the same execution
Inspect the computed usage.users / usage.projects figures written back to each org's document
expectedResult: Org A's usage figures show exactly 3 users / 2 projects; Org B's large counts never bleed into Org A's computed usage, and vice versa.

title: Newly created organization returns zero counts across every module's list/summary endpoint before any data is created
description: Verifies the organization + project creation flow (organization.model.js / project.model.js) never inherits or displays any pre-existing records. This is the platform-wide contract underlying dashboard, risk register, evidence, audit, and vendor empty states.
preconditions: A brand-new organization has just completed signup, with zero projects, evidence, risks, policies, or vendors created
steps: Create a new organization via signup/onboarding
Call GET summary/list endpoints for: risks, evidence, policies, audits, vendors, cloud-posture findings, compliance frameworks (adopted only)
Inspect each response
expectedResult: Every endpoint returns an empty array / zero count for the new org — no records, KPI values, or chart data points originating from any other organization or from platform seed/demo data are present.

title: A second project created within an already-active organization starts with zero data, isolated from its sibling project
description: project.model.js scopes projects by organizationId only — project-level isolation (as distinct from org-level isolation) depends entirely on every controller applying an explicit projectId filter rather than falling back to an org-wide query when projectId is present but the record set is empty for that specific project.
preconditions: Org A has Project X with 10 risks, 5 evidence items, 2 active audits
Org A creates a new Project Y with zero data
steps: Switch active project context to Project Y in the client panel
Load the dashboard, risk register, evidence management, and audit assurance pages
expectedResult: Every page shows zero data / empty state for Project Y — none of Project X's 10 risks, 5 evidence items, or 2 audits appear under Project Y's context.

title: Notification dispatch pipeline delivers audit/risk/policy events only to sockets in the matching org-scoped room
description: vibrantix-backend/src/core/socket.js joins each authenticated socket to `org:${socket.orgId}:user:${socket.userId}` (NOTIF-005) in addition to the personal `user:${userId}` room. This verifies the dispatch → BullMQ → Socket.IO emit pipeline actually targets the org-scoped room for org-wide broadcast events (e.g. policy expiry alerts), not a global unscoped channel.
preconditions: Users from org A and org B both have active Socket.IO connections
An org-wide notification event is triggered for org A (e.g. a policy expiry alert)
steps: Connect one socket authenticated as an org A user and one as an org B user
Trigger a policy-expiry (or audit-completion) notification event scoped to org A
Observe which socket(s) receive the emitted event
expectedResult: Only the org A socket receives the event; the org B socket receives nothing for this event.

title: PDF/Excel report generation renders the requesting org's own name and logo, never a cached prior org's branding
description: Verifies report template rendering is not served from an org-agnostic cache. Guards against TI-014 (report generator caches compiled template metadata, including org name/logo substitutions, keyed without organizationId).
preconditions: Org A (name 'Aventra Corp') generates a compliance report
Org B (name 'Meridian GRC') generates the same report type immediately after
steps: As an org A user, generate a compliance/audit report PDF
Immediately after, as an org B user, generate the same report type
Inspect the header/footer branding on both PDFs
expectedResult: Org A's report header shows 'Aventra Corp'; org B's report header shows 'Meridian GRC' — never the other org's name, logo, or framework selection.

title: Two organizations connecting the same underlying cloud account each see only their own scan findings
description: Verifies cloud_resource / Prowler finding records carry organizationId at ingest time and are queried with an org filter, rather than being attributed only to whichever org most recently triggered a scan of a shared credential set (an MSP scenario).
preconditions: Org A and Org B both register the same test AWS account credentials (simulating a shared/MSP-managed account)
steps: Trigger a Prowler scan from Org A's cloud-posture page
Trigger a Prowler scan from Org B's cloud-posture page against the same account
Compare the findings shown on each org's cloud-posture dashboard
expectedResult: Each org's cloud-posture view shows only findings ingested under that org's organizationId — Org B never sees Org A's finding list or resource inventory, even though the underlying cloud account is identical.

title: ai_policy_generator_python RAG ingestion tags every embedded policy chunk with org_id, and retrieval filters on it
description: Verifies the Python policy-generator microservice's vector store ingestion and retrieval pipeline enforces org-level metadata partitioning end-to-end (ingest → similarity_search with a filter), not just at the assistant-service layer.
preconditions: Org A has an AI-generated policy referencing a unique, distinctive internal control name
Org B requests AI generation of an unrelated policy
steps: As an org B user, request AI generation of a new policy on an unrelated topic
Inspect the RAG context / retrieved chunks used to ground the generation
expectedResult: No chunks from org A's policy documents are retrieved or referenced in org B's generation context.

title: GET /frameworks/adopted returns only frameworks with a client_frameworks record for the caller's org, distinct from global template catalog
description: Verifies the framework picker's two data sources (global templates vs. org-adopted frameworks) are not co-mingled in a way that makes a new org appear to already have ISO 27001/SOC 2/HIPAA active. Grounds TI-013.
preconditions: A brand-new org has adopted zero frameworks
steps: As the new org's admin, open the GRC Framework overview page
Inspect which frameworks are shown as 'active/adopted' vs. 'available to add'
expectedResult: Zero frameworks appear as adopted; all catalog frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2, HIPAA, etc.) appear only under 'available to add', clearly marked isTemplate/isAdopted:false, with no Statement of Applicability content pre-populated.
